
=================================================================
#47 Queen Jinduk  (647 February)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: coronation drama
Logline: The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples. Seungman sits very still while the goldsmith does it, because somebody told her once that Dukman never fidgeted, and she has believed it for forty years.
[1] ¶ Seungman is crowned Queen Jinduk before the blood on the yard dries. The bloodline’s last polite miracle, stamped and filed while the censers are still warm. The succession Bidam died objecting to passes at last. Unanimously.
[2] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 1 (647), 2nd month): Taizong* of Tang sent an envoy bearing his tally to confer on the late queen the posthumous rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and to invest the new queen as Pillar of State and King of Lelang Commandery.❞
[3] [CARD Queen Jinduk]
[4] ¶ Alchun is not at the coronation. The court writes his absence down as illness. Everyone knows the illness’s name. It lasted ten days.
[5] ¶ The court does not mean to compare. It simply cannot stop. The old Queen read the peony seeds before they were planted. She heard frogs at Jade Gate Pond in midwinter and sent two thousand men to the exact valley where five hundred Baekje soldiers were hiding. She named the day of her own death and was right about it. The new Queen is gentle, and good at a loom, and has never once predicted anything.
[6] The Court Maids: The old Queen would have known it was going to rain. / Shh. / …She would have, though.
[7] ¶ After the rites, the new queen keeps two men behind. One of them has not had time to wash the mud off his boots.
[8] Queen Jinduk: Yushin… preserve the sacred country…
[9] Queen Jinduk: Bidam…
[10] ¶ She does not finish the name. Everyone in Surabol has heard what Bidam called him by the end. Gaya. Never of Silla.
[11] Queen Jinduk: Yushin… surely Bidam’s words are not weighing on you…?
[12] Kim Yushin: No — what could there be to weigh on me. / I am a loyal servant of the sacred country.
[13] ¶ He says it the way he says the oath on the yard, every word where it belongs. His right hand has closed on his sword belt and does not open. She grew up beside Dukman. She notices hands.
[14] Queen Jinduk: Then let go of the belt, General. / Nobody here is going to draw on you.
[15] ¶ He lets go. It takes him a moment to remember how.
[16] Queen Jinduk: Chunchu. / Unni knew about the frogs before the frogs did. I can’t even tell when it’s going to rain.
[17] King Muyeol: Majesty, nobody asks the moon to be the sun. / They love it because it lets them look straight at it.
[18] Queen Jinduk: …You had that ready.
[19] King Muyeol: Since the funeral, Majesty.
[20] ¶ Then the border spoils the moment, the way borders do. A runner comes in still wearing the road. Baekje is over the western line again, three forts at once. The court turns to the new queen the way it used to turn to the old one, waiting for her to already know.
[21] Queen Jinduk: I don’t know. / Unni would have dreamed it last week. I didn’t dream anything. I slept badly, that’s all.
[22] Kim Yushin: Give me the men, Majesty. I’ll go. / I won’t need a dream to find three forts.
[23] King Muyeol: He’ll win them back. He always does. / And next spring they’ll come for three more. And the spring after that. / Majesty, we can hold the door forever. We can’t make it stop knocking.
[24] Queen Jinduk: Then what stops it?
[25] King Muyeol: A bigger door. / One man alive has an army that size. He lost a summer at Ansi, and he hates losing. / Let me go west and ask him.
[26] ¶ The old queen would have decided this with a smile, as if she had read it in the stars the night before. The new one has read nothing. She looks at Yushin’s hand, which is back on the belt. She looks at Chunchu, who has clearly had this ready since the funeral too.
[27] Queen Jinduk: Yushin, take the men. / Chunchu, go west. / …If you’re both wrong, I want to hear it from you. Not from a runner.
[28] ¶ Outside, it starts to rain. Nobody predicted it.
[29] The Court Maids: …It’s raining. / Did anybody know? / Shh.
[30] ¶ Nobody says a word about the old queen. For the maids, that is the coronation.
[31] ¶ At night she sits at a loom, because her hands want work that nobody will compare. Three years from now she will weave an ode to the Tang emperor into a length of silk, and it will do more for Silla than any prophecy her cousin made. Nobody at court thinks to compare that.
[32] ¶ **Silla needs an army. Only one man alive can lend it, and he has never lent anything for free. Chunchu goes west…!**
